Hospital Planning Sectional Committee, MHD 14

FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Hospital Planning Sectional Committee had been approved by the Medical Equipment and Hospital Planning Division Council. This is the formal recognition by the community of the social structure of a country and its responsibility for providing the means for keeping them well or restoring lost health. The single doctor clinic including dental clinic has been defined as an integral part of a social and medical system, the function of which is to provide instant curative treatment to population having diseases with low risk of threat to life. In the recent past there has been a mushrooming growth of substandard single doctor clinic including dental clinic in India which necessitated the need of review of position in this regard and put forward suggestions for improving the quality of these clinics through standardization and setting up of minimum norms for extending medical care to common consumer. While formulating this standard, assistance has been derived from the following: Delhi Nursing Home Registration Act, 1953 and Amendment to Rules (1965), issued by Delhi Administration. This standard covers functional requirements, space requirement, continuity of care, infection control, facility management and safety, human resource management etc. The other standards published on the subject, which could also be relevant, are given in Annex A. The composition of Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex B.

IS 15904 : 2010

Indian Standard GUIDELINES FOR SINGLE DOCTOR CLINIC INCLUDING DENTAL CLINIC
1 SCOPE This standard lays down the guidelines for single doctor clinic establishment. The standard covers basic requirements for planning single doctor clinic in respect of functional, space, and management requirements. Certain essential requirements for building, services and environment have also been included. 2 REFERENCES The following standards contain provisions which through reference in this text constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision and parties to agreement based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated below: IS No. IS/ISO 14001 : 2004 IS/ISO15189 : 2003 18001 : 2007 Title Environmental management systems -- Requirements with guidance for use Medical laboratory-- Particular requirements for quality and competence Occupational health and safety management systems requirements seeking treatment at the clinic, toilet facility shall also be catered. 4.2 Clinic Single doctor clinic for any of the required discipline (may be single or polyclinic) shall contain the facilities described here in under. An observation bed may be catered for day care on need basis. 4.2.1 Medical Clinic The clinic should have one or two consultation-cumexamination rooms depending upon the load of patients. The clinic should also have facilities for cardio graphic examination. 4.2.2 Surgical Clinic The clinic should have one or two consultation-cumexamination rooms depending upon the load of patients. The clinic should also have facilities for treatment-cum-dressings. 4.2.3 Orthopaedic Clinic The clinic should include arrangements for plaster preparation fracture treatment besides consultationcum-examination. For X-ray facilities the clinic may have the radiography room within the clinic or outsource the facility. 4.2.4 Eye Clinic The clinic should include consultation-cum-refraction, minor surgery-cum-treatment. For testing the state of refractive power of the eye, room length not less than 6 m is essential. However, by use of mirror length of room can be reduced. 4.2.5 ENT Clinic The clinic should include consultation-cum-treatment and a sound-proof audiometry room. 4.2.6 Dental Clinic The clinic should have facilities for dental consultationcum-surgery, dental hygiene, dental workshop and Xray facilities. 4.2.7 Obstetric and Gynaecological Clinic The clinic should include consulting-cum-examination room, treatment, and clinical laboratory. Antenatal patients have to undergo certain formalities prior to examination by the doctor, clinical laboratory for the 1

3 SINGLE DOCTOR CLINIC 3.1 Single doctor clinic is for curative treatment of patient suffering from seasonal/minor diseases, which has low risk of patient life and available nearby the locality. 3.2 Single doctor clinic is usually operated by one doctor but may be assisted with more professionals in the field. Such doctor's clinic may be either of discipline namely medical, surgical, orthopaedic, eye, ENT, dental, obstetric and gynaecology, paediatric, skin, psychiatry, pathology, radiology, physiotherapy/ rehabilitation, etc. 4 FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS 4.1 General Facilities 4.1.1 Reception-cum-Waiting Lobby At the entrance of the single doctor clinic, a reception cum waiting lobby for the patient should be provided. Depending upon the workload and number of patients

IS 15904 : 2010 purpose is essential. A toilet cum changing close to treatment may also be provided. 4.2.8 Paediatric Clinic The clinic should provide medical care for infants and children up to the age of 12 years. Beside consultation and examination room, the clinic shall be provided with a separate dressing, treatment and immunization room. 4.2.9 Skin Clinic The clinic should provide diagnostic and curative facilities for dermatology, and STD (Sexually transmitted disease). The clinic should include consultation-cum-examination, and a combined treatment room. 4.2.10 Psychiatric Clinic The facilities required for the clinic should include consultation-cum-examination room, and EEG treatment room. Resuscitation (recovery room) may be provided. 4.2.11 Pathology Clinic Single doctor clinics as listed above may require pathology services for diagnostic purposes. It may not be feasible to cater in house facility. On the lines of Single Doctor Clinic, exclusive pathology clinic for the analysis of diseased tissue or fluid and other elements in the body may be established. The facilities required for the clinic should include consultation room, sample collection, and a general purpose laboratory to cover all feasible tests. 4.2.11.1 Laboratory Laboratory should be provided with 600 mm wide and 800 mm high bench of length about 1.6 m per technician. Each laboratory bench shall have laboratory sink with swan neck fittings, reagent shelving, gas and power point and under counter cabinet. Top of the laboratory bench shall be acid and alkali-proof material. 4.2.12 Radiology Clinic Some of the single doctor clinics as identified above particularly orthopaedic clinic may require radiodiagnostic services for conducting radiology examination. It may not be feasible for the clinics to cater in house facility. Like wise single doctor clinic, exclusive radiology clinic to cover the basic needs of X-ray and Ultrasound may be established. The facilities required for the clinic should include consultation room, radiography room, Ultrasound room, and a film developing-cum-processing room. 4.2.12.1 Radiography room The room should have a sub waiting area with a toilet and a change room facility. The radiography unit should be operated from a separate control cabin or behind a mobile protection screen of 1.5 mm lead equivalent. 2 From radiation protection and safety point of view, normal one brick wall thickness is adequate. 4.2.12.2 Ultrasound Ultrasound room shall be provided as necessary. A patient toilet, accessible from the procedure room and from the corridor, shall also be made available. 4.2.12.3 Film developing and processing room A dark room shall be provided for processing film unless the processing equipment normally used does not require a dark room for loading and transfer. 4.2.13 Physiotherapy Clinic Some of the single doctor clinics as identified above particularly orthopaedic clinic may require physiotherapy treatment. It may not be feasible for the clinics to cater in house facility for the purpose. Like wise single doctor clinic, exclusive physiotherapy clinic to provide treatment facilities to patients suffering from crippling diseases and disabilities. Treatments may be classified as physical and electro-therapy, and exercise. The facilities required for the clinic should include consultation room, few cubicles for physical and electrotherapy treatment, and an exercise room. 4.3 Single Doctor Dental Clinic Single doctor dental clinic should be well aerated, well illuminated, spacious and shall be equipped with dental chair unit with accessories like good illumination, basic instruments, spittoon and inlet/outlet water connection and dental X-ray facilities in the basic guidelines of radiography. 4.3.1 Facilities for complete and comprehensive sterilization should be available in the clinic with modern methods of sterilization like autoclave/hot air oven/electrical sterilization and chemical sterilization. 4.3.2 Dental Laboratory The dental laboratory shall have minimum basic equipment required for making or repairing dentures and dental appliances shall be available in the laboratory. It shall be well aerated, well illuminated and spacious. Provision for dust extraction should be there. 5 SPACE REQUIREMENT 5.1 Space Planning Module To facilitate planning and framing of the structural grid, a usable and workable space planning module of 14 m based on basic space unit of 3.5 m has been stipulated in order to rationalize the requirements for various facilities in the single doctor clinic. 5.2 The recommended space requirement for various functions (see 4.2 and 4.3) is given at Table 1.

6 MANPOWER REQUIREMENT For a viable size of single doctor clinic, in the beginning when it starts working, it is recommended that the total strength should be related to nature of facilities catered and patients workload envisaged. 7 INSTRUMENTS REQUIREMENT AND EQUIPMENTS

8.1.3 There shall be a documented established laboratory safety programme. Written policies and procedures shall guide the handling and disposal of infectious and hazardous materials. Further the laboratory personnel shall be appropriately trained in safe practices and shall be provided with appropriate safety equipment/devices. 8.1.4 Imaging services shall be provided as per the requirements of the patients and shall comply with legal and other requirements. Appropriate qualified and trained personnel shall perform and/or supervise and interpret the investigations. Those imaging tests, which are not available in the single doctor clinic (Radiology), shall be outsourced to other agency based on their quality assurance system. 8.1.5 Written policies and procedures shall guide the handling and disposal of radioactive and hazardous materials. Imaging personnel shall be provided with appropriate radiation safety devices, which shall be periodically tested and documented. Personnel shall be trained in radiation safety measures. The imaging signage shall be prominently displayed in all appropriate locations. 8.2 Infection Control 8.2.1 The single doctor clinic should have defined procedure reducing/eliminating infection risks to patients, visitors and providers of care. The infection control programme shall be documented. It shall include equipment cleaning and sterilization practices. 8.2.2 Proper facilities and adequate resources shall be provided to support the infection control programme. Facilities like hand washing shall be accessible to healthcare providers in all patient care areas, and compliance with proper hand washing shall be monitored regularly. 8.3 Facility Management and Safety 8.3.1 The single doctor clinic shall comply with the 4

7.1 The instruments and equipment required by allied single doctor clinic may vary according to the nature of clinic and facilities being catered. The instruments and equipments may conform to the relevant Indian Standards. 7.2 Doctor's consultation-cum-examination room shall be equipped with a doctor's chair, Doctor's table, patient chair/stool, follower's chair, examination couch, wash hand basin, first aid box, clinical thermometer, stethoscope, BP instrument and other appropriate instruments to commensurate with the type of treatment and nature of clinic. 8 MANAGEMENT PARTICULAR REQUIREMENTS 8.1 Continuity of Care 8.1.1 Laboratory services shall be provided as per the requirements of the patients. Scope of the laboratory services shall commensurate with the services provided by the Pathology Clinic and appropriate qualified and trained personnel perform and/or supervise the investigations. The facility for those tests which are not available in the single doctor clinic (Pathology) shall be outsourced to other agency depending upon their quality assurance system and facility available. 8.1.2 There shall be a documented established laboratory quality assurance programme (see IS/ISO 15189). This programme shall address verification and validation of test methods, surveillance of test results, periodic calibration and maintenance of all equipments with documentation of corrective and preventive actions.

IS 15904 : 2010 applicable legislations and regulations and its environment and facilities shall operate to ensure safety of patients, their families, staff and visitors (see IS/ISO 14001). 8.3.2 Qualified and trained personnel shall operate and maintain the clinical and support service equipments. These equipments shall be periodically inspected and calibrated for their proper functioning. 8.3.3 The single doctor clinic shall have provisions for safe water, electricity, medical aid etc. Potable water and electricity shall be available round the clock with alternate sources, which shall be tested on regular basis. 8.3.4 The single doctor clinic shall have a well defined and documented plan for management of hazardous materials and such materials shall be identified within the clinic. The clinic shall implement processes for sorting, handling, storage, transporting and disposal of hazardous material. 8.3.5 Statutory provisions with regard to bio-medical waste management shall be complied with. Biomedical waste treatment facility shall be managed as per statutory provisions (if in-house) or outsourced to authorized contractor(s). Requisite fees, documents and reports shall be submitted to competent authorities on stipulated dates. 8.3.6 There shall be a plan for managing spills of hazardous materials and staff shall be educated and trained for handling such materials. 8.3.7 The single doctor clinic should identify the potential safety and security risks. Ensure development, implementation, and monitoring of the safety plan and policies (see IS 18001). 8.4 Human Resource Management 8.4.1 The single doctor clinic depending upon the facilities available and load of patient should maintain an appropriate number of staff to meet the care, treatment and service needs of the patient as per the norms wherever available. The single doctor clinic shall ensure competency and skill of paramedical and general employees. 8.4.2 There shall be a documented personal record for each staff member. Personal files shall be maintained in respect of all employees. The personal files shall contain personal information regarding the employee's qualification, disciplinary background and health status. 8.4.3 Regular health checks of staff dealing with direct patient care shall be done at least once in a year and the findings/results shall be documented. Occupational health hazards shall be adequately addressed. 8.4.4 There shall be a process to identify job responsibilities and make clinical work assignments to all nursing staff members to commensurate with the qualifications, training and registration and any other regulatory requirements. The services provided by nursing staff shall be in accordance with the prevailing laws and regulations.
